[00:00] Sofia Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, with Liam -- we'll do a quick intro then jump into your current stack and goals.
[00:08] Priya Patel: Hey, thanks, I'm Priya -- lead search at Novacore. We have Ethan, our CTO, and Marta who's our ML engineer.
[00:14] Ethan Brooks: Morning / afternoon all, yeah excited to see what you have.
[00:18] Liam Chen: Great. Can you kick off with your current infra and what you're trying to achieve?
[00:24] Priya Patel: Sure, so right now we run OpenSearch with a BM25 baseline for our product search, and last year Marta led a small embeddings pilot using a 768-d model, stored in an in-house vector store built on top of Postgres. It's kinda kludgy, latency's ok for web, but we see big tail latencies and the throughput doesn't scale. We're aiming to move to a production reranking flow where the embedding-based reranker handles top-K rerank after BM25 and we want predictable latency at scale.
[00:47] Marta Lopez: yeah, and we're seeing issues when QPS hits 3-4k, the nearest neighbors step and disk IO become a bottleneck. We're exploring hosted vector DBs or something we can run dedicated — and also thinking about dimensionality tradeoffs, 1536 vectors look better quality but cost more to store and slower to query.
[01:05] Sofia Ramirez: Makes sense. Typical tradeoffs. Quick qual question: what peak qps and p99 latency target are you aiming for on the rerank stage?
[01:12] Priya Patel: Peak we'd like 6k qps for the top-K retrieval stage, end-to-end rerank under 200ms p95 ideally. If that's too ambitious we could accept 300ms p95 as a phased target.
[01:24] Liam Chen: Got it. And how big is your corpus? Number of vectors, average doc length?
[01:29] Marta Lopez: About 120 million passages right now after chunking, avg chunk length ~120 tokens. Update frequency is daily batch-ing, nearline updates only, we don't need real-time inserts for most use cases.
[01:40] Ethan Brooks: Security wise we need SAML SSO, SOC 2 posture, audit logs, and data residency in us-east for now.
[01:47] Sofia Ramirez: All standard requirements, we have Hosted with SOC2 and regional controls, Dedicated for reserved capacity and Private for VPC/on-prem — we can map those to your needs.
[01:56] Priya Patel: The thing is cost. We're worried Hosted may get pricey at that scale. Can Dedicated help with unit cost?
[02:02] Liam Chen: Yes, Dedicated is intended for predictable throughput and better cost per token / per-query once you commit. There's also autoscaling and burst options. For vector search specifically, Dedicated lets you pin GPU-backed nearest neighbor nodes for faster ANN, and you can control quantization profiles.
[02:20] Marta Lopez: When you say ANN, are you running HNSW or IVF-type indexes under the hood? How does Redwood handle index types and quantization?
[02:28] Liam Chen: We support multiple backends depending on deployment. Hosted uses a managed ANN service with HNSW + product-quantization options; Dedicated gives you more control — we can precompute PQ centroids, use 8-bit or 4-bit quantization on embeddings, and tune recall/latency. For Private you get the same runtime but deployed to your VPC. There are some differences in operator access, but the serving runtime is the same.
[02:47] Ethan Brooks: Ok, important for us is the ability to run hybrid search: BM25 to get candidates, then embedding ANN, and rerank via a model -- we need traceability and explainability, and ability to tune blend weights.
[03:01] Sofia Ramirez: Totally, we see that pattern a lot. You can run hybrid pipelines: route initial candidate generation to your OpenSearch BM25, then call Redwood's embed/retrieval API for top-N ANN, or we can host the ANN layer and accept BM25 candidate lists to rerank. Blend weights and scoring are configurable; we also emit per-request scores and traces for observability.
[03:20] Priya Patel: What about embedding dimensionality? Marta mentioned 1536 vs 128. We've seen quality improvements moving up dims but the cost/latency jump is significant.
[03:30] Liam Chen: Right — higher dims = higher memory and slower ANN ops. Typical approach: run experiments with 1536 for quality baseline, then try quantization (like OPQ + PQ) or dimension reduction techniques for inference. Sometimes teams use 512 or 768 as compromise. Another option is asymmetric hashing or IVF to keep query latency low. We'll help with model recommendations in Redwood Optimize.
[03:50] Marta Lopez: Also curious about throughput: can Redwood handle batch queries? We have many short queries and would want batching to improve GPU utilization.
[03:57] Liam Chen: Yes, our serving runtime does continuous batching and KV cache where applicable. For reranking, batching helps but there's tail-latency tradeoff; Dedicated can be tuned to favor throughput with slightly higher median latency or optimized for low p99 depending on your SLOs.
[04:11] Priya Patel: For the pilot we want to test: 10k qps peak for ANN retrieval stage, 120M vectors, test both 768 and 1536, and run hybrid BM25 + embedding rerank. Can you run a benchmark?
[04:22] Sofia Ramirez: Absolutely. Liam can put together a benchmark script and we can run it on Hosted with dedicated capacity equivalent, or on Dedicated if you prefer an apples-to-apples cost comparison.
[04:32] Ethan Brooks: Which vector DBs have you integrated with if we want to keep OpenSearch in front?
[04:36] Liam Chen: We integrate with OpenSearch, Elastic, Postgres-based stores, Pinecone, Milvus, and also have native ANN in Redwood's runtime. If you want to keep OpenSearch for initial retrieval, that's OK — we can accept candidate IDs and only index embeddings in Redwood or run a sidecar ANN.
[04:50] Marta Lopez: Are there limitations on dimensionality for your hosted ANN? Some vendors cap dims or have performance cliffs above 1024.
[04:57] Liam Chen: Hosted can handle up to 2048 dims, but performance characteristics change; we recommend quantization for >1024 to reduce memory. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the benchmark.
[05:08] Priya Patel: On security, do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs per request? We need that for compliance.
[05:15] Sofia Ramirez: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Hosted has KMS integration options and robust logging, plus SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll send the security pack with SOC2, data flow diagrams, and example logs.
[05:28] Ethan Brooks: For Private deployments, how much ops do we need to provide? We prefer minimal operator burden but may accept a VPC-managed control plane.
[05:36] Liam Chen: Private comes in two flavors: VPC-hosted control plane where Redwood manages control plane but runtime sits in your VPC, or full on-prem where you operate the runtime with our support bundle. There's tradeoff in responsibility vs isolation.
[05:48] Marta Lopez: A practical question: what does the rollout look like for a pilot? How long to get data into the system and run tests?
[05:54] Sofia Ramirez: Typically 1-2 weeks to onboard for a bench pilot: exchange creds, ingest a replica subset (we recommend 5-10M vectors for initial perf tests), run benchmarks, then iterate. For full corpus tests it can take longer depending on throughput.
[06:06] Priya Patel: Ok, so immediate asks: pricing, security docs, and a benchmark plan.
[06:10] Sofia Ramirez: We'll do that. Liam, you'll own the benchmark plan?
[06:13] Liam Chen: Yep. I'll propose scripts, sample queries, and metrics to capture: qps, p95/p99 latencies, recall@k, and cost per query.
[06:22] Priya Patel: Great. Also can you include a suggested config for hybrid scoring and an example of the reranking pipeline?
[06:28] Sofia Ramirez: We'll include an example config and a short demo runbook.
[06:33] Marta Lopez: One more question — do you have a recommended approach for dimensionality reduction if we need to compress from 1536? PCA? Distillation?
[06:40] Liam Chen: We usually recommend distillation to a smaller dimension or OPQ + PQ. For quick wins, you can try PCA or SVD but they sometimes lose semantic nuance. We'll test a few approaches in the benchmark.
[06:52] Ethan Brooks: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side to run the bench?
[06:56] Marta Lopez: We'll need to share a sample dataset and some traffic patterns, and agree on candidate queries. I'll prep an export.
[07:03] Sofia Ramirez: Perfect. We'll follow up with the security pack and pricing.
[07:07] Priya Patel: Thanks, this was helpful.
[07:09] Sofia Ramirez: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Sofia to send pricing + security docs; Liam to deliver benchmark plan and scripts; Marta to share sample index; schedule technical deep-dive next week.
